title: fix(update): keep snapshot watchdog diagnostics
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #177225. Managed-update snapshot watchdog failures could discard the last phase/path and leave the durable failure's stderr empty.

## User Impact

Snapshot failures retain the active phase/source, elapsed time, last progress age, and last database's page/byte counters in the error, saved receipt, and `openclaw update status`. The watchdog now labels its bytes as **total estimated snapshot input, including SQLite and plugins**, rather than implying that one database of that size was being copied.

This repairs the installed updater going forward; a newer staged candidate cannot restore diagnostics already discarded by an older updater. No options, schemas, dependencies, or activation policy change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot supervisor checked cancellation before calling the existing failure formatter, after parsed progress had already been removed from stderr. Phase-only progress was also excluded from receipts. Watchdog cancellation now uses the ordinary-failure formatter after worker settlement, including cancellation while a completed worker's progress receipt drains. The parser preserves the last database counters when a later phase-only event arrives; the canary and receipt/report projections retain the resulting stderr. Process-tree settlement and uncertain-cleanup handling stay intact.

The reported stall matches the sequence in #176813/#176968 (`1d210bb5`): the parent's progress writer could retry a synchronous shared-state authorization snapshot without limit after the child's shared copy completed. That repair already bounds admission attempts and warns when optional progress recording is skipped. The cause of #177225's Raspberry Pi stall remains **unproven** because its report lacks the repeated-worker/write evidence needed to establish identity. This change preserves the earlier repair and covers both a pending progress receipt after the shared copy and a later plugin-inventory stall. Phase-only forwarding overlaps the narrower work in #163463; cancellation formatting and durable stderr complete the repair here.

## Evidence

- Three subprocess regressions failed before the respective fixes and pass afterward: shared-copy timeout, later plugin-inventory timeout, and cancellation after worker exit while a progress receipt drains. They verify redaction, process exit, scratch cleanup, real ledger round-trip, and report rendering. Final case times: 237 ms, 154 ms, and 150 ms.
- Isolated real-worker proof copied a disposable 16 KiB SQLite database, then forced plugin filesystem inspection to stall. The watchdog retained `during plugin inventory`, `Last snapshot: shared database snapshot: completed`, `4/4 pages`, and `16,384 bytes`. The source remained byte-identical; the child exited and scratch was removed. Test time: 13.17 s; wall time: 39.65 s.
- With isolated `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, and config, `pnpm openclaw update status --json --timeout 1` exited 0 and returned those diagnostics in `lastRun.steps[].stderrTail`. Its deliberately short registry lookup timed out without affecting saved history. This was local macOS fixture proof, not a reproduction on Raspberry Pi.
- Core and focused test typechecks, touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, `git diff --check`, and Madge passed (0 cycles). Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. The existing #176968 real-worker regression also passed.
- Initial affected-consumer run: 1,020 passed, 1 failed, 1 preexisting PostgreSQL skip. The failure was investigated and the shared fixture was repaired as detailed below. All 17 remaining files were then selected: 16 files passed (287 tests), and the Windows-only file was skipped on macOS (6 cases). Exit 0 in 282.118 s; no new failures.
- Final pre-publication freshness: `git fetch origin main` observed `0031c6706deaca079e75be9897e62e70389841a2`; #177225 remained open. No additional same-owner fix landed after the integrated Doctor fixture repair. The existing diagnostic-loss mechanism is still unfixed on main.
- The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory step was skipped under the campaign's local gate budget because of its known 20–40+ minute host cost. PR CI supplies broad proof.

### Resume-completion regression repair

The materially higher failure rate on this PR was investigated, not dismissed as inherited. The fixture called Doctor config components without the real Doctor process-custody or maintenance owners. When its 15-second child deadline expired, the parent's receipt still had `pid: 0`, causing `ERR_COMMAND_PROCESS_CLEANUP_UNCERTAIN` despite cooperative process shutdown. It now retains real custody through worker joins and runs config repair/finalization inside the existing state-only maintenance scope. Parent settlement itself took 0–1 ms and handle/receipt cleanup under 50 ms. No snapshot-supervisor or snapshot-progress-formatter calls occurred in the traced resume flow; formatting was not retaining custody.

Fixing custody exposed the interrupted repair: native macOS directory-watch registration could consume the deadline while Doctor discovered configured agent databases. `resolveAgentDir` registered process-lifetime ancestor watchers during a bounded schema-maintenance operation. Traced discovery pauses were 7–18 seconds; one successful child spent 2,411 ms registering 20 watches. A native sample caught Bun's main thread waiting on the watcher lock. The registry now resolves directory identity directly inside schema maintenance, without retaining watcher-backed caches. Normal runtime caching remains. The owner regression also proves immediate symlink-retarget visibility and preservation of the original registered owner. It failed before the fix with 11 native watcher calls (17.38 seconds), then passed in 27 ms with no watches. Deadlines, retries, and existing assertions are unchanged.

Baseline: eight complete-file runs per revision with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-resume-completion.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`, isolated state, unchanged tests/deadlines. Original PR head: `224b1998dbc1d3b24ed4cca3d28ef37f0d76b20e`; clean detached main: `7bf2329213d46ba9b35394c45761d55cb3908f57`.

| Failure | Original PR head | Clean main |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full-file runs with failures | 7/8 | 5/8 |
| Original restored-config case, metadata=false | 7/8 | 1/8 |
| Restored-config companion, metadata=true | 4/8 | 4/8 |
| Doctor-only node-state case | 2/8 | 4/8 |

All baseline failures had the same error: `Doctor processes remain unsettled, data-at-risk` with `custody receipt unavailable`. Baseline repetition wall time: 915.409 s on the branch, 933.346 s on main.

**Final committed head `811d1e438cd6cbb830f574fffd0b711c448937b6`: ten complete-file runs, 10/10 passed, zero failed runs and 90/90 test executions passed.** Same command, pinned Bun and isolated state as the original baseline; no retries or deadline/assertion changes. Total wall time 795.259 seconds; per-run range 75.758–85.193 seconds. The original restored-config case and both previously flaky companions passed all ten runs.

The initial complete-file run after both repairs passed 9/9: node-state 8.321 s; restored-config cases 16.208 s and 14.636 s (each includes two Doctor children); deferred-repair case 16.725 s versus 31–42 s before. The four custody/watchdog sibling files previously passed 79 tests. The new registry owner regression, focused test types, lint/format, and Madge passed; independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issue. The 14 registry consumer files were exercised. One catalog cancellation assertion was repaired after it resolved through the legitimate five-second foreground fallback; it now requests `{ refresh: true, wait: true }`, retaining all abort/join assertions. All three cancellation cases passed (48.93 seconds test duration, 60.73 seconds wall), and independent review was clean.

The Bun registry suite stopped making progress during native watch registration; a sample showed its worker waiting on a native lock while `FSEventStreamStart` waited in `f2d_register_rpc`. Only this lane's process was terminated. On the supported Node runner, the registry/session/worker files completed in 1.98 seconds: 19 passed, two registry instrumentation assertions failed ("Missing agent directory ancestor watch" and zero locally observed watches). The same two assertions failed with unchanged main registry source: nine passed/two failed in 1.13 seconds. Node delegates macOS watching to a child helper, while those assertions observe the caller's `fs.watch`; these are inherited runtime-test mismatches. They are recorded, not claimed green. The other registry-consumer shards passed: gateway methods 85 tests; infrastructure 60 passed/one repaired cancellation failure; CLI 12; commands one; catalog-context four. Normal-runtime native watching remains unchanged.

During freshness, main landed `4b96de6ce8ea`, a separate fix that removes native directory observation from the short-lived Doctor test child. Main was integrated to resolve the fixture overlap, preserving its hook and compiler boundary; the real custody and maintenance lifecycle wraps it. The diagnostic issue remains open. After integration, five focused files passed **80 tests** in 203.38 seconds (watchdog/custody, lease lifecycle, fresh Doctor timeout, and the maintenance regression). Focused test typechecking passed; the merged diff received a fresh clean P0–P2 review. A first compile attempt failed before tests because the worktree still had the old TypeScript package; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` synchronized the isolated install to main’s existing lockfile, then the same proof passed. No dependency declaration was changed by this PR.

<details>
<summary>Preexisting test cost</summary>

The initial consumer run also passed these unchanged, costly fixture suites: `update-command-database-rollback.test.ts` (13 scenarios, 399.638 s summed test time; maximum 55.743 s), `update-command-rollback.test.ts` (46 scenarios, 889.702 s summed test time; maximum 39.039 s), and `update-cli.candidate-activation.test.ts` (14 scenarios, 159.810 s summed test time). `doctor-config-flow.billing-route.test.ts` also passed its seven cases in 168.572 s summed test time (maximum 35.156 s). The registry-consumer run also measured the unchanged catalog overload case at 31.379 seconds and its 64-agent metadata case at 49.417 seconds; both run real worker/agent compositions. These fixtures repeatedly construct isolated installations and run fresh runtime/service/Doctor processes. This is test-body cost, not only shared compiler preparation; reducing repeated fixture boots is a separate owner-level performance task.

</details>

The original ClawSweeper review on `224b1998dbc1` found no actionable defect. Its suggested broader inventory/diagnostic-mode scope is outside this lane and would require new options; the requested diagnostic-loss repair and `Fixes #177225` remain the scope. A fresh review is requested after this update.

**Diff:** production +74/−33 (7 files), tests +287/−31 (4 files), docs +6/−0 (1 file). The necessary growth reuses the existing parser and receipt/report owners; no second watchdog formatter or persistent store.
